plain_language_meaning: PEMF frequency generally refers to how many electromagnetic pulses or cycles occur per second, measured in hertz.
safety_note: Frequency should not be used by itself to imply a specific medical effect or guaranteed outcome.
commercial_relevance: Helps explain what Hz means on PEMF product pages and comparison pages.
notes: Use as the neutral opening definition.

plain_language_meaning: Hertz, abbreviated Hz, means cycles per second. A 10 Hz setting means ten cycles per second.
safety_note: Hz language should remain educational and should not be converted into disease-treatment claims.
commercial_relevance: Useful for customers comparing PEMF mats, pads, and portable devices.

plain_language_meaning: A PEMF device may offer one fixed frequency, several preset frequencies, or an adjustable frequency range.
safety_note: Different devices may define and deliver frequency settings differently, so users should review manufacturer specifications.
commercial_relevance: Helps compare PEMF devices without assuming all frequency settings are equivalent.

plain_language_meaning: Many consumer PEMF wellness devices use low-frequency settings, often described in single-digit or low double-digit Hz ranges.
safety_note: Low frequency does not automatically mean safer, stronger, weaker, or medically effective. Device design and instructions still matter.
commercial_relevance: Useful for explaining common consumer PEMF category language.
notes: Avoid ranking frequencies as universally best.

plain_language_meaning: Frequency presets are built-in PEMF settings selected by the device manufacturer.
safety_note: Preset names should not be treated as medical claims unless supported by intended-use language, evidence, and regulatory status.
commercial_relevance: Helps clarify preset labels on PEMF devices and manuals.

plain_language_meaning: Schumann resonance is often discussed around 7.83 Hz in wellness marketing and PEMF discussions.
safety_note: References to Schumann resonance should not be used as proof that a consumer PEMF setting produces a medical benefit.
commercial_relevance: Useful because users commonly search for 7.83 Hz PEMF meaning.

plain_language_meaning: 7.83 Hz is commonly referenced in PEMF and wellness content because of its association with Schumann resonance terminology.
safety_note: Do not claim 7.83 Hz treats, cures, or prevents disease. Treat it as a frequency reference unless specific evidence and intended-use claims apply.
commercial_relevance: Helpful for searchers comparing common PEMF frequency settings.
notes: Claim-boundary row for a high-interest frequency.

plain_language_meaning: 1 Hz means one cycle per second and may appear as a low-frequency PEMF setting on some devices.
safety_note: Do not assign a universal biological effect to 1 Hz without device-specific evidence and context.
commercial_relevance: Useful for explaining simple PEMF setting labels.

plain_language_meaning: 3 Hz means three cycles per second and may appear as a low-frequency PEMF setting on some devices.
safety_note: Do not assign a universal biological effect to 3 Hz without device-specific evidence and context.
commercial_relevance: Useful for explaining simple PEMF setting labels.

plain_language_meaning: 5 Hz means five cycles per second and may appear as a low-frequency PEMF setting on some devices.
safety_note: Do not assign a universal biological effect to 5 Hz without device-specific evidence and context.
commercial_relevance: Useful for explaining simple PEMF setting labels.

plain_language_meaning: 10 Hz means ten cycles per second and is a commonly discussed PEMF frequency setting.
safety_note: Do not claim that 10 Hz produces a guaranteed effect across all people, devices, or use cases.
commercial_relevance: Useful for common PEMF frequency searches and product education.

plain_language_meaning: 20 Hz means twenty cycles per second and may appear in adjustable PEMF devices or preset programs.
safety_note: Device design, waveform, intensity, session length, placement, and instructions matter along with frequency.
commercial_relevance: Useful for explaining that Hz is only one device variable.

plain_language_meaning: 30 Hz means thirty cycles per second and may appear at the upper end of some consumer low-frequency PEMF devices.
safety_note: Users should follow manufacturer instructions and avoid assuming higher frequency means better results.
commercial_relevance: Relevant to products with 1 to 30 Hz-style frequency ranges.
notes: Good for Holistix PEMF range explanation.

plain_language_meaning: Frequency describes timing, while intensity, field strength, waveform, pulse shape, coil design, and exposure area describe other device characteristics.
safety_note: A device should not be judged by frequency alone. Frequency is only one part of the technical profile.
commercial_relevance: Helps prevent misleading PEMF comparison shopping.

plain_language_meaning: Waveform describes the shape or pattern of the electromagnetic signal over time.
safety_note: Waveform claims should be explained as device specifications, not as proof of medical benefit.
commercial_relevance: Useful for future PEMF product-spec and buyer-guide content.

plain_language_meaning: PEMF intensity or field strength describes how strong the magnetic field is, often discussed separately from frequency.
safety_note: Users should not compare devices by Hz alone because strength and delivery method can differ substantially.
commercial_relevance: Supports more honest PEMF device comparisons.

plain_language_meaning: Session duration is a separate variable from frequency and may affect user experience and safety guidance.
safety_note: This dataset does not provide PEMF dosage protocols. Users should follow manufacturer instructions and consult a qualified professional when appropriate.
commercial_relevance: Prevents frequency education from becoming treatment advice.

plain_language_meaning: PEMF use may require caution for people with implanted electronic devices, pregnancy, seizure history, active bleeding concerns, or other individual risk factors depending on device labeling.
safety_note: Users should review contraindications, follow manufacturer warnings, and consult a qualified healthcare professional when risk factors are present.
commercial_relevance: Connects frequency education to the PEMF Contraindications Database.

plain_language_meaning: PEMF frequency charts can help organize terminology, but they can also overstate certainty when they map each frequency to a specific condition or promised outcome.
safety_note: Avoid rigid frequency-to-disease charts unless supported by appropriate evidence, intended-use language, and regulatory status.
commercial_relevance: Protects Holistix from bad frequency-chart claims while still owning the topic.

plain_language_meaning: Educational PEMF copy should separate frequency terminology, device specifications, safety cautions, user instructions, and medical claims.
safety_note: Avoid disease claims, guaranteed results, unsupported before-and-after promises, and claims that one frequency is universally best.
commercial_relevance: Keeps Holistix open-data assets citation-worthy and lower-risk.

plain_language_meaning: PEMF frequency terminology should be reviewed periodically because device designs, evidence, regulations, and market claims can change.
safety_note: Rows should be updated when stronger safety guidance, regulatory information, or better product-specification standards become available.
commercial_relevance: Supports future version history and dataset audits.
notes: Use for future v1.2 or later updates.
